blogs.title: TAVR after treated PVE: when does the door reopen?
blogs.description: Using this Enterococcus faecalis PVE case as an anchor, we review when transcatheter therapy can be reconsidered after prosthetic valve endocarditis. We outline prerequisites (completed targeted therapy, negative blood cultures, TEE/MSCT without vegetations or paravalvular complications), the heart team calculus against prohibitive surgical risk, and how contemporary ESC guidance (as cited in the case) frames individualized decisions. We also discuss counseling on recurrence risk and why prior infection history should not dominate once cure is established—anatomy, haemodynamics, and lifetime strategy should.

blogs.title: CT or bust: imaging the road to TAV-in-TAV-in-TAV
blogs.description: A practical playbook for CT-first planning in triple-layer valve anatomy. We detail what to measure (coronary heights, sinus dimensions, valve-to-coronary distance, sinotubular junction, neo-skirt height, commissural/leaflet relationships, minimal internal diameter) and how those data drive valve choice, implantation depth, and the decision to skip coronary protection. The post illustrates how modelling the interaction of existing frames and the anticipated landing zone made a high implant feasible and safe in this case.

blogs.title: Third act device selection: why Acurate neo2 and a high implant won the day
blogs.description: Device-platform nuances matter in serial reinterventions. We unpack the rationale for choosing a supra-annular, relatively low-frame self-expanding valve (Acurate neo2) and executing a deliberate high implant aligned to the Evolut leaflets. Key aims: pin prior leaflets to prevent inward folding, preserve effective orifice area, minimize neo-skirt under the coronaries, and enable commissural alignment. We cover fluoroscopic/CT landmarks, pacing and (pre/post) dilatation strategy, and pitfalls (embolization risk, malapposition) unique to high implants.

blogs.title: The gradient that got better: decoding early severe PPM after triple TAVR
blogs.description: Immediate post-implant mean gradient of 67 mm Hg that fell to ~26–27 mm Hg by 1 month and 1 year—what explains this trajectory? We discuss mechanisms in layered frames: early under-expansion, leaflet restriction that improves after post-dilatation and settling, flow normalization with LV remodeling, and Doppler measurement caveats. We review how to interpret DVI/AVA/indexed AVA in multi-prosthesis anatomy, when to observe vs reintervene, and realistic haemodynamic targets clinicians can counsel patients on.

blogs.title: Keeping the doors open: preserving coronary access through layered frames
blogs.description: Coronary reaccess is the Achilles’ heel of TAV-in-TAV-in-TAV. We translate this case’s commissural alignment strategy into actionable steps: CT-based commissural-to-coronary mapping, selecting platforms that facilitate alignment, targeting high implants to limit the neo-skirt, and planning for future PCI through stent cells. We also discuss bailout and future options (selective coronary protection, chimney stenting, BASILICA, and why BVF/BASILICA in triple frames may be limited), plus documentation habits that help the next operator.

blogs.title: Playing the long game: lifetime management after the first TAVR
blogs.description: This triple-TAVR story underscores the need to plan a procedural trajectory from day one. We cover first-valve choices with an eye to redo(s), commissural alignment as a default, strategies to maintain future coronary access, and how to balance haemodynamics vs frame layering to mitigate PPM down the line. We propose a surveillance rhythm (baseline post-TAVR echo, early follow-up, then annual with CT reserved for rising gradients or access planning), and heart team documentation standards to future-proof care.
